extracted.intended_audience: English teachers, literacy educators, and researchers interested in teaching creative writing to students
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and criteria for developing students' creative writing skills in English, including definitions, essential elements, teaching steps, classroom techniques, and assessment-related aspects for educators and program designers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative writing characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative writing is an innovative writing style that highlights narrative, character development, opinions, and non-formal language styles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include poetry, short stories, novels, epics, fairy tales, drama scripts, film scenarios, song lyrics, television scripts, advertising scripts, popular articles, and opinions. Emphasis is on originality, imagination, and stimulating readers' imagination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal/purpose of creative writing
rubrics_metrics.description: The goal of creative writing is to entertain or, in the case of creative nonfiction, to craft persuasive prose and to stimulate readers' imagination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In poetry, imagery conveys abstract concepts like truth, love, and mortality. The activity also supports self-expression, communication of ideas and emotions, and building readers' imaginative engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction from scientific/academic writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative writing is flexible and less rigid than scientific writing; scientific writing follows systematic and standardized rules while creative writing emphasizes innovation and creativity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific/academic/technical writing are examples of non-creative writing. Creative writing can include non-fiction formats when they display imagination, opinion, or narrative elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Six important aspects of creative writing
rubrics_metrics.description: The practice of creative writing involves six important aspects: knowledge, attitude, process, skill, result, and profession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These aspects frame training: knowledge and process (how to write), attitude (motivation and sensitivity), skill (craft), result (product quality), and profession (career development).

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential writer capacities
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative writing requires critical thinking, emotional sensitivity, talent, and imaginative power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These elements must be stimulated through pedagogy and practice to facilitate the creative process and produce engaging works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation and planning for writing projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparation involves deciding to embark on a writing project, determining goals, researching historical or factual data, and creating a disciplined writing habit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask what you want to achieve and how; change mindset and character to immerse in the project; select genres that may challenge habits, perspectives, or attitudes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set clear learning objectives and indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Teachers must ensure objectives are clearly defined so materials and discussion are focused and students gain solid understanding of effective writing techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear goals enable guidance on writing personal letters, journals, narratives from interviews, etc., and inform assessment and instruction design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduce diverse creative writing genres
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce students to various genres such as short stories, poetry, dialogue sketches, fairy tales, comics, scripts, and popular articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Genre exposure helps students find apt forms for their ideas and develop specific craft elements (e.g., diction in poetry, dialogue for drama).

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a supportive classroom environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Foster discussion, collaboration, freedom of expression, and acceptance of multiple viewpoints in students' writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage risk-taking, provide positive and constructive feedback, and hold reading sessions and performances to build confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular practice and habit formation
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a habit of writing regularly — even a few words or paragraphs daily — to build creative writing skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discipline and consistent practice are essential; motivation and routine help sustain long-term improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading widely as research
rubrics_metrics.description: Reading diverse literary works is key to producing creative writing; reading acts as research and inspiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage making summaries, reviews, and analyses; reading provides references, ideas, and vocabulary to inform original work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of writing prompts and authentic formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilize prompts or authentic partial texts (e.g., a beginning and middle to finish) to spark creativity and practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authentic writing formats and stimuli (video, song lyrics, prompts) provide scaffolds; examples include video storytelling where students predict and then write, or using song lyrics to inspire stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach effective writing techniques (imagery & language)
rubrics_metrics.description: Teach use of imagery, descriptive writing techniques, and creative language choices (e.g., crisp language for popular texts, standard language for educational texts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show how visual language explains scenes without detailing everything; tailor language choice to audience and purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the five senses to evoke vividness
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate touch, sight, smell, hearing, and taste to create vivid sensory experiences for readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While sight, touch, and hearing are common, taste and smell can powerfully evoke memory and emotion; use senses selectively for impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit use of adjectives and rely on strong nouns/verbs
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid overusing adjectives and adverbs; prefer imaginative word choices and concrete nouns/verbs to make prose more engaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Over-reliance on adjectives flattens writing; show examples of replacing adjectives with evocative nouns/verbs or figurative language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use similes and metaphors judiciously
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ similes ('like' or 'as') and metaphors to create unique comparisons and enrich imagery, but avoid cliché and overuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metaphors are especially useful to begin creative writing; ensure comparisons feel fresh and purposeful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include dialogue to animate scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: Use dialogue to keep stories dynamic, convey emotions, reveal character, and prevent monotony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dialogue deepens story and provides context; balance dialogue with description to maintain flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid exaggeration and imbalance in plot/detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not overdo plot elements which can bore readers; likewise, avoid under-detailing scenes which leaves readers unsatisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for proportionate detail: combine descriptive and dialogue techniques to engage readers without overwhelming them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generate original ideas and unique perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Strive to produce distinct, unique messages and approaches rather than repeating common arguments or tropes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop thoughts independent of preconceived notions; gain insight via reading, direct experience, sensitivity to events, and critical analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select a captivating title
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose an alluring title that signals content and piques reader curiosity from first glance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Titles function as labels for works or chapters; invest effort to craft titles that attract attention and reflect the piece's core.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision, proofreading, and iterative drafting
rubrics_metrics.description: After completing a first draft, re-read and revise repeatedly to improve flow, point of view, language, and structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers should be willing to change or remove inappropriate words/sentences; seek feedback from peers and revise until polished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback and peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Be receptive to constructive criticism from friends, peers, or instructors to improve the quality of writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use feedback to inform revisions; classroom peer review and guided teacher feedback are central to skill development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of multimodal and alternative stimuli (video, song lyrics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate media like video storytelling and song lyrics as pedagogical tools to spark ideas and engage students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities include pausing videos to predict outcomes, writing guesses, reflecting on character lessons, and using song lyrics to inspire original works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early introduction and scaffolded instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce writing lessons at an early age (elementary) to build foundational reading and writing skills and foster future creative development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early scaffolding prevents later learning difficulties; incorporate age-appropriate imaginative tasks and progressive instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foster a writing culture and opportunities for public sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Create extracurricular activities, contests, reading performances, and publication opportunities to motivate students and showcase work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing and public performance boost self-confidence, create pride, and can provide economic or reputational incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching sequence (ten-step classroom process)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested teacher steps: introduce genres; create supportive environment; teach techniques (imagery, language); showcase examples; assign regular work; allow freedom of expression; involve students in editing/revising; provide constructive feedback; hold readings/performances; encourage publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These steps provide a scaffolded, systematic approach to classroom creative writing instruction to develop skills progressively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment-related indicators (originality, spontaneity, imagination)
rubrics_metrics.description: An essay or creative piece can be deemed successful if it meets criteria such as being original, spontaneous, and imaginative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment should consider creativity, ability to express ideas clearly, research where appropriate, and development of language and vocabulary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of teacher: guide, set objectives, and model techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Teachers should provide clear objectives, model writing techniques, give constructive feedback, and design appropriate learning models aligned with objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid inappropriate learning models that don't align with objectives; teachers enable student independence beyond classroom through systematic instruction and guidance.
